name: Turn funding newsletters into a scored call list with Bright Data, GPT-5.6, data tables and Gmail

parameters.content:
## Turn funding newsletters into a call list before the round goes cold

You are already subscribed to the newsletters. This reads them the morning they arrive, works out which of the funded companies look like your buyer, and emails you the shortlist with a reason to call each one.

### How it works

A Gmail filter puts your funding newsletters on one label. When one lands, **`Pull Out The Rounds`** extracts every company, amount and stage from the prose - a model, not a regex, because the same round is written three different ways in three different newsletters.

Companies already in the `funding_seen` table are dropped **before** any lookup happens, so the second and third newsletter to cover the same round cost nothing. Whatever is left gets a Bright Data search and a read of its home page, then a fit score against the buyer description you wrote in **Settings**.

**`Route By Fit`** sends the strong ones to your inbox and files the rest on a watch list. A newsletter with nothing new in it ends at **`Nothing New This Issue`** and sends no mail.

### Setup

1. A Gmail credential, and a Gmail filter putting the newsletters on a label. Put that label name in **Settings**.

2. Bright Data, as a Header Auth credential. The free tier is 5,000 credits a month with no card.

3. An OpenAI credential.

4. A Data Table called `funding_seen` with columns `company_key`, `company`, `amount_musd`, `stage`, `tier`, `score`, `angle` and `first_seen`.

5. Describe your buyer in **Settings** in one sentence. That sentence is the whole scoring rubric, so it is worth writing properly.

## 1. The inbox is the trigger
A Gmail filter puts your funding newsletters on one label. Nothing arrives, nothing runs, nothing is spent.

## 2. Prose, read as prose
"raised $12M Series A" and "closes a $12 million Series A" are the same round. A schema handles that; a regex does not.

## 3. Drop the repeats before spending on them
Three newsletters cover the same raise over four days. Checking the table here makes the second and third free.

## 4. Find the company, not the coverage
The top result for a funded company is a news story about the round. Publishers are dropped so the page read is their own.

## 5. Their own words
A zero-length body is a fetch that failed, not a company with nothing to say, so it is marked absent rather than scored as a blank.

## 6. One sentence is the whole rubric
The buyer description in Settings is what the score is measured against, so it is worth writing properly.

## 7. Decide once, route once
The tier was worked out in code above. The Switch only carries it out, so the thresholds live in one place.

## 8. One mail, not one per company
The upsert emits an item per company, so the digest carries `executeOnce` - without it Gmail sends the same mail six times.

## A newsletter is not a filing

Funding newsletters get numbers wrong, round off, repeat rumours and occasionally cover the same raise twice at different amounts. Everything here inherits that. The amount and stage are good enough to sort a call list by and are not good enough to put in a CRM as fact.

The fit score is also an opinion formed from one home page and a search result, not a qualification. It is there to order your morning, not to decide who is worth talking to.

If a company matters, open the round and check it before you use a number in front of the customer.

assignments.name: buyer_description
assignments.value: Series A to Series C B2B software companies in the US or Europe with a sales team of ten or more, who sell a product rather than a service.
